analysis.title: US Pulse: higher rates needed despite stock market weakness
key_insights: ANZ maintains that the FOMC should tighten further despite the recent selloff in stocks, because incoming data argue for more monetary restraint. It expects a 25bp hike in December.
Q3 GDP rose 3.4% saar. Real final sales to private domestic purchasers rose 4.9% saar, the strongest pace since Q2 2021.
October nonfarm payrolls rose 165k and the 3-month average rose to 137k after August and September were revised up by a cumulative 84k. The unemployment rate fell to 4.1%.

Average hourly earnings rose 0.4% m/m in October and September was revised up to 0.3% m/m from 0.1%. Annual wage growth is 3.1%, which ANZ says is consistent with 2.0% inflation given strong productivity growth, but wages bear watching.
Q3 nonfarm productivity rose 3.6% saar, with output up 3.7% and hours broadly unchanged. Productivity has grown at a 2.2% annualised rate since late 2019, against 1.5% in the prior upswing.

The selloff in technology and AI stocks has raised concerns about the AI build-out. ANZ says a severe negative growth shock looks unlikely because most state moratoriums cover new applications and do not revoke existing approvals.
Planned US AI spending for 2027 is estimated at USD1.1-1.4trn, up from USD800bn this year.
Short-term AI financing risk: falling stock prices raise the cost of equity capital and wider credit spreads raise the cost of borrowing. Persistent weakness could also hit consumption.

The Democrats won both Houses of Congress in the midterms. ANZ reads it as a protest over cost of living and the Middle East conflict, with datacentre build-out concerns also a factor. More state AI legislation is expected but should not derail the build-out.

October CPI is due this week. ANZ forecasts headline and core each +0.3% m/m, which would imply 4.0% y/y headline and 2.9% y/y core. The BLS will not publish October y/y rates because October 2025 data are unavailable after the shutdown.

The Bloomberg median expects October PPI final demand at +0.4% m/m, easing from September's energy-driven 1.3%. Commodity costs are feeding into core producer goods prices and fuel costs into transportation services.
Existing home sales are expected to fall 3.5% m/m in October after a 1.5% rise. Mortgage lock-in continues to suppress inventory and transactions.
NY Fed President Williams said last week that now is an opportune time to gather more information. ANZ expects the Fed to have enough information after the October CPI data.

sector_views.rationale: The sharp selloff raises concerns about the pace of the AI build-out and its financing. ANZ expects 2027 AI capex of USD1.1-1.4trn and does not expect a severe growth shock.

tension_points.bull_case: Strong data support another hike. GDP rose 3.4% saar, payrolls rose 165k, the unemployment rate is 4.1% and productivity rose 3.6%, so ANZ expects a 25bp hike in December.
tension_points.bear_case: The AI and tech selloff raises the cost of equity capital, credit spreads are widening, and sentiment among large stock holders fell 5.0%. This may be feeding the Fed's gradualist approach.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A weak October CPI print would undercut the case. ANZ expects the Fed to have enough information after that release.
